decisive_items: Avid irregular enhancement within the right cavernous sinus and enlargement of the right side compared with the left
Biopsy of posterior left pleural thickening showed CD5+, CD10−, non-germinal center B-cell type
response.rationale: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome is the most likely diagnosis due to the patient's symptoms of headache, diplopia, and cranial nerve palsies, along with the imaging findings of irregular enhancement in the right cavernous sinus. While diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is a possible diagnosis based on the biopsy results, the clinical presentation and imaging findings are more consistent with Tolosa-Hunt syndrome.

rejected.why: Sphenoid sinusitis is less likely due to the lack of other symptoms and the presence of air fluid levels in the sphenoid sinuses is not specific enough to support this diagnosis.
Giant cell arteritis is less likely due to the normal inflammatory markers and the lack of other symptoms such as jaw claudication or visual loss.
Sarcoidosis is less likely due to the lack of other symptoms and the presence of lymphadenopathy is not specific enough to support this diagnosis.
Metastatic prostate cancer is less likely due to the lack of other symptoms and the imaging findings are not specific enough to support this diagnosis.
